Real Estate Consultant in Largo & Pinellas County

Navigating the real estate market can feel overwhelming, especially when life throws you a curveball. As a trusted real estate consultant serving Largo, Clearwater, St. Petersburg, and all Pinellas county, we help homeowners understand all of their options — not just the traditional listing route. Whether you’re trying to figure out the best way to sell, want to understand what your home is worth in today’s market, or need guidance on a complicated situation like probate or a distressed property, we’re here to give you straight answers with no pressure and no sales pitch.

Foreclosure Service — Stop Foreclosure Fast

If you’re behind on mortgage payments and worried about losing your home, you’re not alone, and you likely have more options than you think. Our foreclosure service helps Pinellas County homeowners find a fast, dignified path forward before the bank takes control. We can often close a cash sale in as little as 7 to 10 days, which may be enough to stop foreclosure proceedings, protect your credit, and put money back in your pocket. Time is critical with foreclosure, so reaching out early gives you the most options.

Property Investment Company Serving Largo & all Pinellas County

Largo Home Buyers is a local property investment company that buys residential properties directly from homeowners throughout Pinellas County. Unlike national iBuyers or corporate flippers, we’re a real local business based right here in Largo at 1101 S. Belcher Rd — and we have a genuine stake in the community we invest in. We buy single-family homes, duplexes, inherited properties, distressed homes, and landlord-owned rentals. When you sell to us, you’re working directly with a local investor who can move fast, pay fair, and make the process simple from start to finish.

House Clearance Service — Sell As-Is, We Handle the Rest

One of the biggest things that holds people back from selling is the stuff left behind — furniture, junk, decades of belongings, or a home that’s simply been neglected. Our house clearance service means you don’t have to lift a finger. We buy properties in any condition and take care of cleanout, haul-away, and cleanup as part of the deal. Whether you’re dealing with an inherited home full of belongings, a hoarder situation, or just a house that needs a serious cleaning before it’s livable — we’ve seen it all and we handle it so you don’t have to.

How to sell your house fast in Largo: what the timeline really looks like

If you need to sell your Largo house quickly, you probably have a date on the calendar you are trying to beat. Seven days is real, but it is not automatic. We have closed Largo houses in a week and we have had some take five weeks, and the difference almost always comes down to title and paperwork, not the house itself. Here is the honest breakdown so you can figure out where your property lands before you call anyone.

Real closing timelines in Pinellas County

7 to 10 days

You are the only owner on the deed, the mortgage is current or paid off, and there are no tenants. We order title, Gulfside Title Services runs the search, and we close. Most of that week is the title company waiting on payoff letters, not us.

14 to 21 days

There is a lien, back taxes, an old code violation, or a second owner who has to sign. None of these kill a sale. They just add the time it takes to get a payoff figure or track down a signature. We handle the chasing.

30 to 45 days or longer

The house is in probate and no personal representative has been appointed yet. Florida probate has steps that no buyer can skip, and any company promising you seven days on an unopened estate is not being straight with you. We can still start the process now so the sale closes the day the court clears it.

What slows a sale down in Largo specifically

Largo is not one market. West of Belcher, toward Walsingham and Indian Rocks, flood zone status and insurance history come up in almost every deal. Central and east Largo rarely have that problem. If your house is in a flood zone and took water in a storm, the City of Largo runs its own substantial damage review using a 50% threshold, while unincorporated Pinellas County and a few cities, including St. Petersburg, use 49%. Either way, once repair costs cross that line the house has to be brought up to current flood code, often by elevating it. That changes what a retail buyer can do with the property and is a big reason some listings sit for months.

A few other things we see constantly:

  • Mobile and manufactured homes. Largo has a lot of them. We buy these only when the land comes with the home. If you rent the lot in a park, we are not your buyer, and we will tell you that on the first call instead of wasting your week.
  • Old permits that were never closed out. A water heater or roof permit left open years ago shows up in title and has to be resolved. Common, fixable, adds days.
  • Out of state heirs. If you inherited a Largo house and live somewhere else, you can sign remotely. You do not need to fly down.

When selling fast is the wrong call

If your house is in decent shape, you have no deadline, and you can handle a few months of showings, listing with an agent will usually net you more money. We will say so. The reason people come to us to sell their house fast in Largo is almost never price. It is a foreclosure date, a job that starts in three weeks, an estate nobody wants to keep paying taxes on, or a repair bill bigger than the equity. If none of those describe you, go list it.

FAQs: Selling Your House for Cash in Largo & Pinellas County

Q: Who buys houses for cash in Largo, FL?

A: Largo Home Buyers is a locally owned company that buys houses for cash throughout Largo and all of Pinellas County. We’re a small group of local partners led by Doug and Matt, real people who live and invest here, not a national corporation or call center. We buy single-family homes, duplexes, inherited homes, distressed properties, and landlord rentals in any condition.

Q: How fast can I sell my house in Largo or Pinellas County?

A: If the title is clear, we can close in as little as 7 to 10 days. Liens, a second owner who has to sign, or an open probate add time, and we will tell you which applies on the first call. You pick the closing date, so if you need more time to move, that works too. We will give you a fair cash offer within 24 to 48 hours of seeing the property.

Q: Do I have to pay any fees, commissions, or closing costs?

A: No. You pay nothing. There are no agent commissions, no listing fees, and we cover all closing costs. The offer we agree on is the amount you walk away with, minus any existing mortgage or liens on the property.

Q: Do I need to make repairs or clean before selling?

A: No. We buy houses as-is, in any condition. You don’t need to repair anything, paint, clean, or even remove your belongings. Leave what you don’t want and we handle the cleanout as part of the deal.

Q: Can I sell a house with hurricane or flood damage in Largo?

A: Yes. We buy storm-damaged houses as-is, including homes with roof damage, water damage, mold, or a gutted interior. You don’t need to make repairs or file anything with the city first. If your house is in a flood zone and took water, pay attention to the substantial damage rule. The City of Largo uses a 50% threshold, and unincorporated Pinellas County uses 49%. If repair costs cross that line, the house has to be brought up to current flood code, which often means elevating it. That can make the home very hard to sell to a regular buyer. We factor all of this into our offer, so you can sell the house as it sits and move on. Call us and we’ll walk through your options, even if you already received a substantial damage letter.

Q: How do you decide what to offer for my house?

A: We base every offer on real market data: recent comparable sales in your neighborhood, the home’s condition, and the cost of repairs it needs. We walk you through the math so you understand exactly how we arrived at the number. There’s no black-box algorithm and no pressure to accept.

Q: Is your offer firm, or will you lower it later?

A: Our offer is firm but we’ll do our best to meet your goals and work to give you the best offer available. We give you a real number after we’ve actually seen the property, not an inflated phone quote we walk back later. Be careful with companies that give a high offer sight-unseen and then lowball you at the table. That tactic is called bait-and-switch, and it’s exactly what we don’t do.

Q: Will I really get a fair price selling for cash?

A: A cash sale typically nets less than a full retail listing, and any honest buyer will tell you that. What you trade for a slightly lower price is speed, certainty, zero fees, zero repairs, and no risk of a deal falling through. For many sellers, after you subtract agent commissions, repairs, holding costs, and months of waiting, a cash offer comes out very close. We’ll show you both scenarios so you can decide what’s actually best for you.

Q: Can you help me stop a foreclosure in Pinellas County?

A: Often, yes. If you’re behind on payments, a fast cash sale can close before the bank completes foreclosure, which may protect your credit and put money back in your pocket. Time matters here, so the earlier you reach out, the more options you’ll have.

Q: Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished in Florida?

A: In many cases, yes, depending on where the estate is in the probate process. Florida probate has specific steps, and we’ve helped many families navigate selling an inherited Pinellas County home. We can talk through your situation and point you to the right path.

Q: What if there are liens or back taxes on the property?

A: We handle these case by case. Liens and back taxes can usually be paid out of the sale proceeds at closing, so they often don’t stop a sale at all. Tell us what’s on the property and we’ll find a solution.

Q: Can I sell if I still owe money on my mortgage or owe more than the house is worth?

A: Yes. If you have a normal mortgage, it gets paid off from the sale and you keep the rest. If you owe more than the home is worth, we can still talk options, including situations where a short sale or other arrangement makes sense. Don’t assume you’re stuck.

Q: Can I sell a house that still has tenants in it?

A: Yes. We buy tenant-occupied rentals and review the existing lease as part of the purchase. You don’t have to evict anyone or wait for the lease to end before selling.

Q: What happens to all the stuff left in the house?

A: Leave it. Our house clearance service means we haul away furniture, junk, and decades of belongings as part of the deal. Whether it’s an inherited home full of possessions or a property that’s been neglected, you don’t have to lift a finger. 

We’ve cleaned out some pretty nasty houses, so don’t worry about it, we’ll take care of it.
